qualifying_updates.factual_summary: GitHub announced a public-preview server-to-server authentication path for organization-installed GitHub Apps using the Copilot SDK. The app receives read-only Copilot Requests permission and a short-lived installation token; organization model policies, budgets, spending controls, app-attributed usage reporting, and revocation through suspend or uninstall apply.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Treat long-running or automated coding-agent workloads as workload-owned identities rather than as a developer's durable session. Define least-privilege scopes, short-lived credentials, owner-controlled revocation, organization budget boundaries, and app-attributed audit evidence before enabling unattended execution.
qualifying_updates.upstream_routing_note: The product and SDK release belongs to the upstream AI wiki. This downstream artifact preserves only the workload-identity, revocation, budget, and auditability implications.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: GitHub made Copilot assisted permissions generally available in the CLI, Copilot app, and VS Code. A model classifies requests to run commands, access file paths, or open URLs; clearly safe requests proceed automatically while other requests need approval. Enterprise controls can block Allow All, disable assisted permissions, and choose a policy-constrained default for new sessions.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Permission assistance is not a substitute for a team action policy. Specify the approval boundary for commands, filesystem paths, URLs, and session defaults; centrally prevent unrestricted modes where required; and retain manual approval as the fallback for prohibited or unavailable defaults.
qualifying_updates.upstream_routing_note: The feature release belongs to the upstream AI wiki. The retained downstream lens is policy-defined permission escalation and manual-approval fallback.
